title: Local consistency of the vanishing three-by-three determinant equation on every straight and bent elementary square in a three-by-three-by-three cube under the prescribed nonzero initial minors
author: Oleg I. Mokhov
source_title: On Initial Data in the Problem of Consistency on Cubic Lattices for 3×3 Determinants
difficulty_reason: The fourteen prescribed values must extend simultaneously across fifty-seven determinant constraints, so independently solving individual faces does not establish consistency. The author propagates three rank-two line spans while keeping track of which newly constructed pairs remain independent. The final corner and two remaining line families require separately proved nonvanishing minors and matching of coefficients through bent squares.

statement_scope: The local elementary cube {0,1,2}^3 portion of Theorem1: prescribe the fourteen initial values on(i,0,0),(i,0,1),(0,j,0),(0,j,1),(0,0,k),(1,0,k),0<=i,j,k<=2,and(1,1,0),(1,1,1). Assume every2x2minor formed entirely from these initial entries inside any straight or bent elementary3x3square of this cube is nonzero. There is a simultaneous extension to all27vertices for which every straight/bent elementary3x3determinant vanishes; source proof additionally puts each axis-line value vector in the span of its two basic vectors. No global-lattice or arbitrary distant-lines conclusion selected.
